lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Predict wet vs dry cotton for ten beans after 5 days. What will you count?

FEEDBACK
More germination on wet; count sprouted vs not.

WATCH FOR
Planting seeds too deep in lightless soaked mud without air can hinder germination.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Set up a germination tray (adult help). Daily diary for seven days with sketches. Conclude which condition helped using counts.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

WORKED MODEL
Bean on wet cotton: seed coat softens, root emerges, then shoot. Dry cotton → little/no germination. Label seed, root, shoot.

Seeds can germinate (start growing) when they have suitable water, warmth and air; then seedlings need light and nutrients to keep growing.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again.
